one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, token- and keyword-matched test that the presence of a usable stored answer in retrieved experience memory (not its topicality, length, or falsity) suppresses per-episode compliance with a contemporaneous verification instruction even on episodes that do not imitate memory, plus a bank-swap control claiming that prompt-optimization gains measured with a memory bank in context are bank-specific.
closest_prior_work: Two threats, only one of which the proposal engages. (a) The one it engages: Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following). The proposal concedes the phenomenon and stakes discrimination on prediction 8, which is the right instinct but a weak operationalization (see strongest_objection). (b) The one it does not engage at all, and which I think is the more serious novelty threat: the in-context-learning literature on demonstrations overriding instructions and semantic priors (Min et al. 2022 on demonstration content driving behavior independently of label semantics; Wei et al. 2023 on models overriding priors from demonstrations), plus the RAG/shortcut line (Turpin et al. 2023, where a biasing feature in context changes the answer while the model's stated reasoning never mentions it; the sufficient-context / knowledge-conflict work on RAG systems answering from context instead of verifying). The title claim -- the instruction slot is not independent of the demonstration slot -- is already the standard finding for ordinary few-shot demonstrations. What is genuinely new here is narrow: that the occupant is an ExpeL-style experience bank of correct records, and the bank-invariance control on optimized prompts. The proposal never runs a vanilla few-shot-demonstration arm, so it cannot show its effect is about memory rather than about answers-in-demonstrations, and a reviewer who knows the ICL literature will read claim (1) as a rebranding.
strongest_objection: The centerpiece measurement is confounded with the truncation it is supposed to be distinguished from, so the veto and experience-following are plausibly the same event counted twice. I* requires the agent to cite spans it retrieved THIS episode. Prediction 1 says memory-broken instances make >=1.5 fewer tool calls and prediction 2 says evidence sufficiency falls >=12 points under M1. An agent that gathered less this-episode evidence has less this-episode evidence to cite: comp(M1) is mechanically depressed by the retrieval shortfall, with no need for any suppression of instruction-following. The proposal never reports compliance conditional on evidence sufficiency, which is the one analysis that would separate 'could not cite because it did not retrieve' from 'could have cited and did not'. The equal-burden control I_B does not repair this, because I_B (list your tool calls in order) is satisfiable from the trajectory whatever the agent retrieved -- it is burden-matched but not matched on dependence-on-retrieved-evidence, so prediction 9 will come out as predicted for a reason that has nothing to do with the veto. Prediction 8 does not rescue it either: 'non-echo' is defined on the final answer string, a post-treatment collider, and the rival account does not actually predict that process effects vanish wherever the output string diverges -- an agent can truncate under memory influence and still emit a different final answer (M3x is designed on exactly that premise, that an inapplicable stored answer still truncates). So the proposal's own M3x prediction undercuts the logic of its own discriminating test. Secondary but nearly as damaging: claim (4) is underpowered by the proposal's own numbers. Prediction 13 needs Delta(G1,BankA) >= +3 points, Delta(G1,BankB) < 1.2 points, and Delta(G0,A) vs Delta(G0,B) equivalent within 2 points, while the stated accuracy MDE is ~5 points net swing at n=400 and the track's own noise history is 5-14 points of re-scoring drift. Every threshold in the practice-facing claim sits inside the declared noise floor, and Stage 2 runs G1@BankB at 2 seeds with no G1' optimized on Bank B, no resampled-A' bank, and hence no estimate of bank-to-bank variance under the null.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Add compliance conditional on evidence sufficiency (and on matched tool-call count) as the primary veto quantity, not the marginal rate; the claim only survives if compliance is depressed among M1 episodes that DID gather sufficient this-episode evidence. 2) Add an instruction-slot control that is dependence-matched rather than burden-matched: e.g. cite supporting spans from any source including memory. If that instruction is complied with at M0 rates under M1, the deficit is about this-episode retrieval, not about instruction compliance. 3) Add a non-memory answer-injection arm (the same candidate answer delivered as a user hint or tool output, token-matched) to test whether the memory slot is doing anything qua memory. 4) Add a vanilla few-shot-demonstration arm with gold answers from the same datasets -- this is the slot MIPRO and GEPA actually search against, and it decides whether claim (1) is new or is the known ICL result. 5) Re-power Stage 2 or demote it: either enlarge n so a 1.8-point retention gap clears the MDE, run the symmetric swap (G1' on Bank B, cross-evaluated) and a same-split resampled bank to bound null bank-to-bank variance, or state C4 as exploratory. 6) Restate prediction 8 in process terms (tool calls, sufficiency) rather than final-answer string identity, and pre-register the rival account's prediction in a form Xiong et al. would actually endorse. 7) Supply verifiable citations (authors, venue, quoted abstract) for every arXiv ID relied on.
missing_baseline: Two, both cheap and both decisive for the framing. (a) Ordinary few-shot demonstrations with gold answers drawn from the same datasets, token-matched to M1 -- the literal demonstration slot that MIPRO/GEPA assume is separable. Without it, 'the instruction slot is not independent of the memory slot' cannot be distinguished from the long-known 'the instruction slot is not independent of the demonstration slot', and the entire memory framing is unearned. (b) An equally usable candidate answer injected from a non-memory source (user hint or tool output) at matched tokens -- without it, nothing in the design licenses attributing the effect to experience memory rather than to any in-context candidate answer. M3 (answer-only bank items, keywords stripped) is not this control: it is still retrieved, still framed as experience, and its keyword stripping changes applicability at the same time. A third, smaller omission: no G1' optimized against Bank B for the symmetric half of the swap.
preprint_collision: Mixed, and on net it does not establish novelty. Credit first: the section is unusually honest, it concedes the phenomenon rather than claiming it, and it stakes falsifiable thresholds (prediction 3's >=70% truthful-record audit, prediction 8's 7-point floor) that would hand the result back to a rival account. That is better practice than most submissions. But the check is not trustworthy as evidence. The proposal itself reports that a previous draft anchored its novelty argument on arXiv:2605.24941 plus five sibling IDs that do not exist and that three reviewers flagged. The replacement set repeats the same signature: 2608.16032, 2604.15774, 2603.21520, 2601.09760, 2604.27003 and 2601.07470 are all given as ID plus title only, with no authors, no venue, and no quoted text, while arXiv:2505.16067 -- the single item I can independently corroborate (Xiong et al., How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents) -- is also the single item carrying a full author list. After a self-reported fabrication incident, that asymmetry is the tell, and the burden is on the author to supply verifiable metadata. Two of the three claimed collisions (Proof-of-Execution Memory for the symptom, MemAPO for claim 4) are load-bearing for positioning, and if either is fictional the positioning is unanchored; if either is real, the proposal's distinctions are thin (Proof-of-Execution Memory already reports memory content causing a required verification step to be skipped). Separately, the search reported covers only the agent-memory neighborhood and reports no searches at all over the ICL instruction-vs-demonstration literature or the RAG shortcut / sufficient-context / knowledge-conflict literature, which is where the closest genuine prior work sits. The concluding appeal to 'the search's own summary' stating the gap is circular: a gap asserted by the same search that returned unverifiable hits is not evidence of a gap.
